engagementRatePercent.description: (likes + comments) / followers * 100. Null when the post is skipped.

isOutlierHigh.description: Whether the rate is far above the sample's average.

isOutlierLow.description: Whether the rate is far below the sample's average.

skipReason.description: Why the post is left out of the averages: `likes_hidden`, `comments_hidden`, `likes_and_comments_hidden`, or `owned_by_another_account` (a collab posted by another account). Null when it is counted.

items.description: One sample post's contribution to the audit.

posts.description: The latest posts the audit sampled (up to 12), newest first. Empty when engagement can't be calculated.

mediaType.description: `image`, `video` or `carousel`. Null groups posts of unknown type.

items.description: Average engagement of one type of post.

contentSegments.description: Average rate by post type. Empty when engagement can't be calculated.

ownedByAnotherAccount.description: Collab posts on the grid owned by another account, left out because their engagement comes from that account's audience.

sampleCoverage.description: How many of the recent posts had usable engagement counts.

dataFreshnessNote.description: The dates the sample covers. Null without posts.

insight.description: Best-effort AI narrative over the audit. Null for a private or missing profile, and when generation was unavailable or failed; it never blocks or fails the request.

requestId.description: Unique request identifier for tracing this API call.

version.description: Public API version that served the response.

audit.formulaDescription: Engagement rate = (likes + comments) ÷ followers × 100, averaged across recent posts with visible counts.
audit.dataFreshnessNote: Based on recent posts between 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-11.

insight.headlineInsight: Engagement is low for an account of this size, and one carousel carries most of it.
insight.engagementAssessment: The 3 sampled posts average a 0.25% engagement rate against about 291 million followers, with a median of 0.03%. The carousel reached about 0.7%, while the photo and the Reel stayed near 0.01% to 0.03%.
contentPatternObservations: The carousel earned the highest rate in the sample; the Reel and the photo were far behind it.
risksAndCaveats: Only 3 posts were sampled, so treat the rates as directional.
Rates use the public like and comment counts at the time of the call.
recommendedExperiments: Publish more carousels and compare their rate with single photos.
Test whether captions that ask a question lift the comment-to-like ratio.
Repeat the audit after the next five posts to see whether the pattern holds.
